name: Damnation A.D.
label: Revelation
lede: While Ken Olden was playing fast youth crew in Battery, he was tuning down to C in the same D.C. house for a darker band that loved The Cure as much as Crowbar.

eras.title: A studio project with a tagalong singer
eras.text: Ken Olden was already a D.C. straight edge fixture, playing in Battery alongside Brian McTernan. Damnation began as Olden's studio project out of the ashes of Worlds Collide, and Brian's brother Mike, who'd never sung in a band, ended up at the microphone.

q: I have zero musical ability. I do what Ken tells me.
years.src: No Echo · Performer Mag · Gut Feeling
years.h: Ken Olden and Mike McTernan start Damnation in D.C.
years.p: Ken Olden plays every instrument himself at first. Mike McTernan, who met Olden through his brother [[Brian McTernan|eda2cb2f-b2c6-4e74-9fd7-49ea52df4172]], starts out as a tagalong and becomes the singer.
years.xp:
Olden and guitarist Hillel Halloway had played together in Worlds Collide and wanted something heavier. Olden played drums for the band's live shows for nearly a year before he got off the kit and onto guitar, and he says that's when things clicked.

McTernan has never pretended to be the musician in the band.

years.p: Another punk band already called itself Damnation, so Ken Olden and Mike McTernan add the A.D. to avoid the confusion.

eras.title: Two Steps Down
eras.text: Damnation A.D.'s debut came out on Jade Tree, whose co-founder Tim Owen went to high school with Mike McTernan. They made it in the same house they lived in, with drums in an attic bedroom, and toured it with Ignite and Earth Crisis.

years.src: Gut Feeling (Ken Olden) · Wikipedia · No Echo
years.h: No More Dreams of Happy Endings · Jade Tree
years.p: Recorded over a month at Ken Olden's SNP Studio in D.C., in the house the band lived in. The opener, Two Steps Down, is named for the detuning: Damnation played in C.
years.xp:
Alex Merchlinsky's attic bedroom was the drum room, for its wood. Olden wrote most songs on drums first and ran everything through a 50-watt Marshall JCM800 and a Turbo RAT. The influences were Drive Like Jehu, Unwound, Girls Against Boys and [[The Cure|69ee3720-a7cb-4402-b48d-a02c366f2bcf]].

A 45-second Chopin Funeral March had appeared on early 7"s, including a split with Walleye; the CD has the whole piece, placed as a palate cleanser. [[White Zombie|cfe572bf-840f-4bed-934a-f69f4b1e90d4]]'s Jay Yuenger told Olden Time Does Not Rest had one of the sickest riffs he'd heard.
play: No More Dreams of Happy Endings

years.p: Damnation A.D.'s second Jade Tree release, a year after No More Dreams of Happy Endings.
Mike McTernan fights bad stage fright, sometimes throwing up before sets, and says it all goes away after the first line. His favorite memories are 3 a.m. Denny's runs with the other bands.

eras.title: Inner Ear, and then it was time
eras.text: Damnation A.D. moved to Revelation for their second album and cut it at Inner Ear, with D.C. hardcore royalty in earshot. It came out, and the band ended the same year.

years.src: No Echo · Revelation Records pressing history · Hardcore Punk Wiki
years.p: Recorded at Inner Ear, where Mike McTernan sang knowing [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]] could hear him. Wait for a Day opens on a synth.
years.xp: Revelation's first pressing was just 223 copies on grey vinyl. A 2023 collector's rundown of the Revelation catalog called it apocalyptic and way ahead of its time.

q: I think it was just time.
years.h: Damnation A.D. break up after Kingdom of Lost Souls
years.p: Ken Olden was busy with [[Better Than a Thousand|9a5d50be-8dff-4f2f-8852-aa4eafb8f985]]. Mike McTernan says he'd spent years putting off dealing with his mental health.
years.xp: McTernan later joined When Tigers Fight in Springfield, Massachusetts. Working with Olden on that project is what brought the two back together.

eras.title: Better Than a Thousand and When Tigers Fight
eras.text: With Damnation A.D. done, Ken Olden played in the youth crew revival band Better Than a Thousand, using the exact same amp, guitars and settings, just a different tuning. Revelation kept the last album around.

years.h: Revelation's final press of Kingdom of Lost Souls
years.p: 331 copies on orange vinyl, billed as the last pressing. It wasn't.

eras.title: Back, with Fall Out Boy on the record
eras.text: Damnation A.D. reunited on Victory Records and loaded the comeback with guests, including two members of Fall Out Boy.

years.h: In This Life or the Next · Victory Records
years.p: [[Pete Wentz|26cea341-dfab-483f-9cdb-8de82da81019]] and [[Patrick Stump|563abe5e-06b1-430d-99d4-7abf981c6e5a]] of Fall Out Boy guest on If You Could Remember, Wes Eisold on Don't Feel a Thing, and Earth Crisis's Karl Buechner and Darkest Hour's John Henry appear too.
years.xp: McTernan said the guests were people who had influenced him to start playing music again. The video for Knot came out the same year.
play: In This Life or the Next

years.h: Ken Olden and Mike McTernan reunite Damnation A.D.
years.p: Nine years after the split, Olden and McTernan are back as Damnation A.D., playing shows behind In This Life or the Next.

eras.title: Twenty-five years of Pornography
eras.text: Revelation brought Kingdom of Lost Souls back in bigger numbers than ever, and Olden and McTernan finally finished the project they'd been talking about since the start: all of The Cure's Pornography, tuned down even further.

years.h: Revelation re-presses Kingdom of Lost Souls on white
years.p: 1,012 copies on white vinyl, more than four times the 223-copy first pressing from 1998.

years.src: Record Store Day · Gut Feeling (Ken Olden)
years.h: Damnation A.D. cover The Cure's whole Pornography album
years.p: A Record Store Day LP of 800 copies on clear blue vinyl, conceived 25 years earlier and worked on in secret. Olden drops the top string to A# for it.
years.xp: The Cure's 1982 album was one of the band's founding influences. It was Damnation A.D.'s first new release in a decade. Olden says there are still finished Damnation songs sitting around without vocals or lyrics.
